purpose: Sulfasalazine is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis, ulcerative colitis, and Crohn's disease. It helps reduce inflammation and pain in your joints and digestive tract. It can also help keep these conditions from getting worse over time.
how_it_works: Sulfasalazine works by calming down inflammation in your body. It breaks down in your gut into two active parts — one that fights inflammation in the intestines and one that helps quiet your overactive immune system. Think of it like a two-in-one helper that tells your body to stop attacking itself so aggressively.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, headache, and dizziness are the most common issues, especially when you first start. Your urine or skin may turn a harmless orange-yellow color — don't be alarmed! Taking it with food and plenty of water can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you are allergic to sulfa drugs or aspirin. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, blood disorders, or G6PD deficiency. It can make you more sensitive to sunlight, so wear sunscreen. It may lower your body's ability to fight infections, so let your doctor know if you get a fever or feel very unwell. Avoid if you are in the last stage of pregnancy or breastfeeding without medical advice.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual starting dose is 500 mg once or twice a day with meals, then gradually increased to 1,000 mg two to four times a day depending on your condition. Your doctor will adjust your dose slowly to help your body get used to it and reduce side effects. Always take it with a full glass of water.
